reform with steam only, add CO2 later
props.statement: Because of this requirement it is desirable to react the natural gas with steam only and to add the required CO2 later in the production process.

props.name: 1-2 % CH4 in synthesis gas no objection for methanol synthesis
props.statement: For the methanol synthesis 1-2 % CH4 in the synthesis gas is no objection.

props.name: CO2 assumed available
props.statement: In this scheme the CO2 is assumed to be available (it can be recovered from flue gases, e.g. by absorption in ethanolamine solutions).

props.name: dry purification preferred for low sulfur concentrations
props.statement: For low concentrations of sulfur compounds the dry method is to be preferred because of its low cost; for large gas quantities with high sulfur content wet purification is preferred.

props.name: dry-tower purification chosen
props.statement: For this purpose the dry-tower method is most suitable, because of the small amounts of sulfur compounds, its small ground area, and the lower time and labour to renew the mass.

props.name: iron oxide with 6-7 % chromic oxide converts organic S to H2S
props.statement: Organically bound S can be converted into H2S and the H2S then bound as metal sulfide; this conversion takes place at high temperature, already at atmospheric pressure, with iron oxide containing 6-7 % chromic oxide as catalyst.

props.name: methanol synthesis requires H2/CO of 1:2 (as printed)

evidence.note: OCR 'H2ICO' for H2/CO; printed '1:2'; quote withheld: sha256:5ae4de25c3f83456d2e7c041f9fd3b36c188df31c05104fe6b2b0029c731a852 chars:41

props.statement: The methanol synthesis requires an H2/CO of 1:2 (as printed); the steam-CH4 reaction gives a gas with too much H2 for this synthesis, and adding CO2 to the steam can regulate the H2/CO ratio. In this design the CO2 is supplemented later in the synthesis gas.

props.name: the natural gas contains very little sulfur

evidence.note: OCR 'c5;. rdgas' for aardgas; quote withheld: sha256:d3864c4ab91638d52031dd180d9222e4ded950ef3d3da3ee1db1515bdb219105 chars:95

props.statement: The material balance of the purification equals that of the preheater, because the natural gas contains only very little S.

props.name: estimated Dutch methanol demand 4000 ton/year
props.statement: The Netherlands' need for methanol is estimated at 4000 ton/year, including further processing to formaldehyde, hexamethylenetetramine and penta-erythritol, based on estimated imports in 1952.

props.name: design basis: methanol plant of 50 ton per day
props.statement: The report gives the calculation of a synthetic methanol plant with a daily production of 50 ton.

props.name: gas-purification design: 52,41 kmol/hr, 10 cm/sec, contact time 4,5 sec, two towers of four 45 cm layers
props.note: the contact time is taken from references 30, 31, 32
props.statement: 52,41 kmol/hr of natural gas is to be purified over four layers (iron oxide, zinc oxide, iron oxide + zinc oxide, used Ni-catalyst mass); gas velocity in the layers 10 cm/sec, contact time 4,5 sec, layer thickness 45 cm; two towers each with four layers of 45 cm, height about 4 m.

props.name: reformer catalyst of the design: Ni impregnated in 0.75 in ceramic cubes, space velocity 500 at 850-1260 °F
props.statement: The catalyst to be used consists of nickel impregnated in 0.75 in cubes of ceramic material; the space velocity is 500 at a temperature of 850-1260 °F.

props.name: soda-iron oxide catalyses the oxidation of organic S; about 0.2 % oxygen needed
props.statement: Organic sulfur can also be removed by the soda-iron oxide method (used by the Germans during the Second World War in the Fischer-Tropsch processes): the soda-iron oxide catalyses the oxidation of the organic S compounds to sulfur oxides, which are bound by the soda; about 0.2 % oxygen must be present in the gases.

props.name: sulfur (H2S or organic S) is harmful to reformer and methanol-synthesis catalysts
props.statement: Sulfur, occurring as H2S or as organic S, is harmful to the reformer and the methanol-synthesis catalysts; it is therefore removed from the natural gas.
